headline: Tech rout fuels haven bid: 2-year yield drops 11bp, gold tops $4,100, oil rebounds on tanker attacks
summary: An AI-led stock selloff sent investors into Treasuries, pulling the 2-year down about 11bp to 4.47% and the 10-year 5bp to 4.84%, and helped Comex gold settle above $4,100. Oil reversed part of Wednesday's 8% collapse, with WTI up 2.7% to $90.52 as new tanker attacks revived supply worries. Bunds touched a two-month low, while OATs lagged during a French national strike.
drivers: AI selloff drives a haven bid into the front end

The Nasdaq 100 fell about 6% and roughly $2 trillion of tech value was wiped out as traders feared the Democratic Congress will slow data-centre building. The 2-year fell about 11bp to 4.47% and the curve bull-steepened, even though jobless claims dropped to 189,000 vs 197,000 expected.
Tanker attacks put a floor under oil

UKMTO logged at least five vessel incidents since Sunday and the IRGC said two tankers caught fire near Hormuz, while drones hit Russia's Ryazan refinery. WTI settled +$2.40 at $90.52 and Brent +$3.67 at $98.29, with ULSD up 3.5%.
Gold extends its rebound; silver lags on tech

Comex gold settled +1.0% at $4,102.50, the highest since Oct 21, on lower yields and haven demand, but gave back a $4,146 peak late. Silver rose only 0.2% to $52.23 as the chip rout hit its industrial story.

Hammack and Barkin both backed gradual further hikes and the BoE raised rates to 4% with one vote for 50bp. Bunds fell to near 3.24%, a two-month low, but OATs stalled near 4.77% during a nationwide strike after the budget's defeat.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled +$2.40 (+2.7%) at $90.52, snapping a three-day slide; Jan Brent +$3.67 (+3.9%) at $98.29.
oil.why: After Wednesday's 8% collapse took WTI to its lowest since Aug 31, fresh tanker attacks put supply risk back in the price: UKMTO logged at least five incidents since Sunday, and the IRGC said two tankers and a tug caught fire using unauthorised Hormuz routes. Ukrainian drones hit Russia's Ryazan refinery, Iran's negotiating stance was unchanged, and Eurasia Group cut its deal odds to 10% from 20%, so traders bought back part of the lost premium.
oil.outlook: Expect choppy two-way trade in an $86–95 range: the midterm result keeps a lid on escalation risk, but shipping attacks stop the premium from draining fully. A close above $94 would point to renewed escalation; a break under $86 needs a concrete US–Iran deal.
oil.watch: Hormuz shipping incidents, US–Iran talk headlines, Russia–Ukraine–US talks Nov 10–11 and EIA stocks Nov 12.

gas.note: Dec RBOB rose 3.48¢ (+1.3%) to $2.7634, bouncing off a near-eight-month low; AAA pump average $4.10, down 12¢ in a week.
gas.why: Gasoline followed crude's rebound but lagged it, so the crack narrowed: diesel led the barrel, with ULSD up 3.5% to $4.35 as Ukraine's drone strikes on Russian refineries threaten diesel exports. Gasoline's own picture is softer, with winter-grade blends, finished refinery maintenance and post-summer demand easing, and the AAA average falling to $4.10 from $4.22 a week ago, though still more than $1 above last year.
gas.outlook: Bias sideways to lower between $2.65 and $2.90 as pump prices keep catching down to futures and winter blends cut costs. Only a renewed crude spike above $94 WTI would lift RBOB back toward $3.
gas.watch: Crude and Hormuz headlines, EIA gasoline stocks and refinery runs Nov 12, and the AAA average approaching $4.

gold.note: Comex Nov settled +$41.40 (+1.0%) at $4,102.50, the highest since Oct 21; spot hit $4,146 before easing to near $4,090.
gold.why: Gold extended its post-election rebound as a tech and AI stock rout, with the Nasdaq 100 down about 6%, sent money into havens and pulled the 2-year Treasury yield down 11bp. Some rate-futures measures pushed the next Fed hike toward March, and falling unit labour costs eased inflation fears. Gains faded late in London as the dollar steadied on hawkish Fed comments and jobless claims of just 189,000.
gold.outlook: Bias modestly higher in a $4,050–4,200 range while real yields fall and equities stay fragile; resistance sits at $4,146 and the $4,190–4,230 moving-average band. A strong payrolls print that firms December hike odds above 80% would risk a slip back toward $4,000.
gold.watch: US payrolls Fri Nov 6, US CPI Tue Nov 10 and the dollar's reaction to Fed speakers.

silver.note: Comex Nov settled +11.3¢ (+0.2%) at $52.23; spot faded late to near $51.75 as equities slumped.
silver.why: Silver lagged gold because it is half an industrial metal: the AI and chip selloff, with chip stocks posting their second-worst day on record, hits the data-centre and electronics demand story that had backed silver. It still held most of Wednesday's 5% jump, helped by lower yields and haven demand, but the gold/silver ratio widened back toward 79 as gold outperformed.
silver.outlook: Range trade between about $50 and $54.50 with a slight downside tilt while tech stocks look for a floor; it needs a recovery in risk appetite to break higher. A close below $49 would retest the late-October low.
silver.watch: Payrolls Nov 6, the tech-stock rebound or lack of it, and China demand signals.

us2y.note: Down about 11bp to near 4.47%, the biggest drop on the curve, as the tech rout pushed back Fed hike pricing.
us2y.why: An AI-led selloff, with chip stocks posting their second-worst day on record and about $2 trillion wiped off the Nasdaq, sparked a haven bid and made traders doubt the Fed can keep tightening into falling equities; some rate futures pushed the next full hike toward March. The rally came despite strong data, as jobless claims fell to 189,000 vs 197,000 expected, and Hammack and Barkin both backed further gradual hikes.
us2y.outlook: Bias lower toward 4.35–4.40% if equities keep falling, but the Fed's hawkish tone limits the rally; 4.60% is the level that would signal hike pricing is back. Payrolls and CPI decide the next 10bp.
us2y.watch: October payrolls Fri Nov 6 (consensus about 59,000), CPI Tue Nov 10 and more Fed speakers.

us5y.note: Down about 8bp to near 4.61%, the lowest in roughly two months, as the belly followed the front end.
us5y.why: The 5-year tracks the expected path of Fed hikes over the next few years, so it rallied hard as the equity rout and a softer oil premium led traders to scale back 2027 tightening. Strong claims and hawkish Fed speakers cut the move from its intraday best, but the haven bid dominated as the S&P 500 fell about 3%.
us5y.outlook: Bias lower in a 4.50–4.70% range while risk assets wobble; a hot CPI or strong payrolls would push it back toward 4.70%. Next week's 3-year and 10-year refunding auctions add supply.
us5y.watch: Payrolls Nov 6, CPI Nov 10 and the refunding auctions next week.

us10y.note: Down about 5bp to near 4.84%, the lowest close in almost two months; 2s10s steepened to near 37bp.
us10y.why: The 10-year extended Wednesday's 6bp rally as the AI-led stock selloff sent investors into Treasuries, and lower oil since the weekend has eased inflation fears. It lagged the 2-year because the curve bull-steepened: traders cut near-term Fed hike pricing faster than long-run inflation and deficit premiums. Claims at 189,000 and gradual-hike comments from Hammack and Barkin capped the rally.
us10y.outlook: Bias lower in a 4.75–4.95% range while equities stay under pressure and oil stays below $95; 4.75% is the next support. A strong jobs report or hot CPI would send it back above 4.90%.
us10y.watch: Payrolls Fri Nov 6, CPI Tue Nov 10 and the 10-year auction next week.

us30y.note: Down about 2bp to near 5.26%, lagging the front end as the curve steepened.
us30y.why: Long bonds rallied least because the move was about the Fed path, not long-run inflation. The haven bid helped, but a falling front end steepens the curve, and investors still demand a premium for heavy issuance and sticky inflation. The Democratic sweep points to gridlock and less new spending, which helps at the margin.
us30y.outlook: Range of 5.15–5.35% with a steepening bias; the long end is likely to lag any further rally. A move above 5.35% would need a hot CPI or a weak 30-year auction.
us30y.watch: Payrolls Nov 6, CPI Nov 10 and the 30-year refunding auction next week.

de2y.note: Little changed to about 1bp lower near 2.96%, as December ECB hike bets held despite global bond gains.
de2y.why: Schatz yields barely moved because ECB pricing is anchored by October's 4.0% euro-area inflation, the highest since 2023, and recent hawkish ECB comments. Lower oil and the US rally helped the long end more, while the BoE's hawkish 8-1 hike, with one vote for 50bp, reminded markets that European central banks are still tightening.
de2y.outlook: Range of 2.90–3.05% with a December ECB hike largely priced; a sustained oil drop below $85 Brent would be the trigger to unwind some of it. Bias flat.
de2y.watch: ECB speakers, euro-area wage data and the ECB meeting Dec 17.

de5y.note: Down about 2bp to near 3.03%, a two-month low, following Treasuries and lower oil.
de5y.why: The belly gained as the Treasury rally and the global tech selloff spilled into Europe, where tech stocks fell over 4% and ASML lost about 7%. A softer oil premium eased some inflation worry, but hawkish ECB pricing after the 4.0% October inflation print limited the move, unlike in the US.
de5y.outlook: Bias slightly lower in a 2.95–3.10% range while risk assets are weak; a hot US CPI or an oil rebound above $100 Brent would push it back above 3.10%.
de5y.watch: US payrolls Nov 6, US CPI Nov 10 and ECB commentary.

de10y.note: Down about 1–3bp to near 3.24%, the lowest since late August, as the global bond rally continued.
de10y.why: Bunds tracked Treasuries and lower energy prices to a two-month low as the AI-led equity selloff boosted demand for safe assets. The rally was smaller than in the US because the ECB is still seen hiking in December, with euro-area inflation at 4.0%. The BoE's hawkish hike and a midday oil rebound also slowed gains.
de10y.outlook: Bias lower toward 3.15–3.20% if equities stay weak, in a 3.15–3.35% range. A Brent move back above $100 or hawkish ECB comments would send it back to 3.30%.
de10y.watch: US payrolls Nov 6, US CPI Nov 10 and the ECB Dec 17.

de30y.note: Little changed near 3.63%, holding near a three-month low as the long end lagged the belly.
de30y.why: The 30-year held Wednesday's gains near its lowest since mid-August. Lower oil and the haven bid helped, but long-end supply, German fiscal expansion and a steepening global curve kept buyers cautious. Equity weakness supported duration, but the long end gained less than the 5- and 10-year.
de30y.outlook: Range of 3.55–3.72% with a steepening bias; heavy issuance limits the rally. A break above 3.72% would need an oil spike or a hawkish ECB shift.
de30y.watch: German auctions, US data Nov 6 and Nov 10 and global long-end supply.

fr2y.note: Little changed near 3.48%, as a national strike offset the global bond rally.
fr2y.why: Short OATs held steady as ECB hike pricing anchored the front end and French politics stayed tense: the Assembly unanimously rejected the first part of the 2027 budget late Wednesday, and Thursday's nationwide strike over pay and the cost of living drew large crowds. The global rally gave support but did not push yields lower.
fr2y.outlook: Range of 3.40–3.55%; the front end mostly follows the ECB, so a dovish turn after a sustained oil drop is the main downside trigger. Bias flat.
fr2y.watch: French protest follow-up, the Senate budget debate and the ECB Dec 17.

fr5y.note: Little changed to about 1bp lower near 4.16%, lagging Bunds as French politics weighed.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT gained less than Bunds as the budget defeat and the national strike kept French risk in focus. The government's original bill now goes to the Senate, with a vote set for Dec 9, and the risk of more cuts or rule by decree keeps investors wary. Global bond strength stopped yields from rising.
fr5y.outlook: Range of 4.05–4.25% with spread risk skewed wider into the Senate process; a clear path to a 2027 budget would bring 4.05% into play.
fr5y.watch: French protests, Senate budget timetable and rating reviews.

fr10y.note: Little changed near 4.77%; the spread to Bunds held near 153bp as the strike offset the global rally.
fr10y.why: After tightening about 10bp on Wednesday on lower oil and the Treasury rally, the OAT–Bund spread stopped narrowing as France faced a nationwide strike a day after the Assembly unanimously rejected the 2027 budget's first part. With growth near zero and the 5% deficit target at risk, investors were reluctant to chase OATs even as Bunds hit a two-month low.
fr10y.outlook: Range of 4.65–4.90%, with the spread likely held in a 145–160bp band; a budget passed even by decree could tighten it toward 140bp, while wider unrest or a government crisis would send it back above 160bp.
fr10y.watch: Strike follow-up, the Senate budget debate and the Dec 9 Senate vote.

fr30y.note: Little changed near 5.33%, still close to its highs as fiscal risk kept the long end heavy.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT barely joined the global rally because long-dated French debt carries the most fiscal and political risk. Thursday's strike and the failed budget vote keep investors demanding extra yield for deficits near 5% of GDP and debt above 115% of GDP, and a steepening global curve did not help.
fr30y.outlook: Range of 5.20–5.45% with a bias to underperform shorter OATs; a credible budget deal could pull it toward 5.20%, while political escalation risks a retest of the highs.
fr30y.watch: French politics, Senate budget debate and OAT auctions.

watch: Next: US October payrolls Fri Nov 6, US CPI Tue Nov 10, Russia–Ukraine–US talks Nov 10–11, the Treasury refunding auctions and EIA stocks next week, the French Senate budget vote Dec 9 and the ECB Dec 17.
